item.title: Downton Abbey spoof is silly and funny
item.description: In “Fackham Hall” a new porter forms an odd bond with the youngest daughter of a well-known English family, as they deal with the epic disaster of their eldest daughter’s wedding. Source: Australian Catholics.

item.title: France in shock over murder of young convert
item.description: The alleged murder at the hands of far-left activists of a young Frenchman who had converted to Catholicism has caused profound shock in France. Source: EWTN News.

item.title: Catholic leaders call for Lenten prayers amid drought
item.description: Catholic leaders across Eastern Africa are urging prayers and action this Lent for millions facing a deepening drought crisis. Source: OSV News.

item.title: Strong employment figures could result in another rate rise
item.description: Australia’s unemployment rate held steady at 4.1 per cent for January with nearly 18,000 jobs created, according to data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics released on Thursday. Source: SBS News.

item.title: Victoria’s upper house reverses High Court decision on Church liability
item.description: Victoria’s upper house has passed the Vicarious Liability Bill unopposed, reversing a High Court decision that found the Catholic Church could not be sued for the actions of a priest. Source: ABC News.

item.title: International study links ‘doomscrolling’ to suicide
item.description: An international study has identified a link between screen time, suicide and self-harm in adolescents. Source: Australian Catholic University.

item.title: Pope will be on the move in 2026
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will visit ground zero of Europe’s migration drama, the Sicilian island of Lampedusa, and also minister to Italians poisoned by years of toxic dumping by the mafia, according to travel plans announced on Thursday by the Vatican. Source: Crux.

item.title: ‘Deep sense of peace’: Bishop-elect prepares for new chapter in his life
item.description: As Bishop-elect Mark Freeman prepares for his episcopal ordination and installation as Bishop of Ballarat on March 19, the desire to fully embrace this new chapter in his priestly vocation is foremost in his mind. Source: Hobart Archdiocese.

item.title: Brisbane Archdiocese backs antisemitism bill, questions curbs on free speech
item.description: Brisbane Archdiocese is voicing support for a new Queensland bill targeting antisemitism and terrorism that increases penalties for people interrupting Masses, assaulting priests and stealing from churches, but questions sections targeting free speech and religious freedom. Source: The Catholic Leader.
